summary: Ryuken Nawa works in Indology and Buddhist studies. In 2026, he was attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Ryuken Sato (1930–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2014, he was attested as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an adviser at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.
Ryuo (1856–1926) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He taught at Koyasan University and served as an educator at Tō-ji.
Ryusei Keira works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his thesis at the University of Lausanne in 2003 under the doctoral supervision of Tom Tillemans.
Ryushin Kitao (born 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He was attested as a professor at Shuchiin University in 2014 and 2026.
Ryushin Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was attested as a professor at Bukkyo University in 2015 and as a faculty member at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

Ryushin Sudo (1929–2018) studied at Taisho University around 1948–1953, specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) studied at Ryukoku University (~1951–1957) in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute (attested 1962) and was a professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1975–2003).

Ryusho Hikata (1892–1991), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He was a professor and dean at Kyushu University and president of Fukuoka Women's University.

Ryuta Kikutani (born 1978) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and Kyoto University (attested 2020), and was attested as an associate professor at Koyasan University in 2026.

Ryutaro Tsuchida (born 1947) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo and under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg. He was an assistant at Marburg (~1980–1983) and became a professor and professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo.

Takayoku Kimura (born 1947) studied at Komazawa University in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1978), a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).
Ryuyu Saito works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.
Ryuzan Nishimoto (1891–1974) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1916, he studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa.
Ryōmin Akizuki (1921–1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1944–1948). He held a post at Saitama Medical University from around 1972 to 1991.

Rüdiger Schmitt (born 1939) is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1961–1965) and served on the faculty at Saarland University from circa 1968 to 2004.
S. A. S. Sarma is an Indologist who held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, attested in 2004 and 2024.
S. Bhaskaran Nair worked in Indology at the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, where he held posts as general editor (attested 1944, 1992) and deputy director (attested 1974–1977, 1986).

S. D. Laddu (1926–2021) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He was attested at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1968 and served as editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).
S. Ghosh worked in Tibetology. In 1982, Ghosh was attested as a librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and as an editor for the Bulletin of Tibetology.
